title: Modern turn-based strategy game with AI (solo developer, open sourced)
author: Icy-Requirement5701
selftext:
I built a modern-day (WW3-style) grand strategy game (browser based). It’s fully open-source if anyone wants to explore it or build on top of it (link is in the about section of the menu).

I’m a casual strategy player and a developer, so this was an experiment to see how far I could push something like this using AI in a short time. It took about 2 weeks from inception to launch. 

**AI in the workflow**

Used different tools for different roles:

* ChatGPT → design and gameplay
* Claude → planning and all coding
* [Scenario.gg](http://Scenario.gg) → all asset generation (images, videos, graphics)

  
**Tech stack**

* React + TypeScript + Vite
* Zustand for state
* Voronoi-based province generation
* Canvas 2D renderer + some Three.js
* Fastify + [Socket.IO](http://Socket.IO) backend

  
**Playable** **demo**: [https://fracturepoint-web-client.vercel.app/](https://fracturepoint-web-client.vercel.app/)  
*Best experienced on desktop - not optimized for mobile*

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: Dude this is awesome! I can't wait to see what it evolves into, I wish I was at home to try it out

comments.author: mechbasketmk3
comments.body: This look amazing!  Nice job.  For Scenario.gg, is it worth it?

replies.author: Icy-Requirement5701
replies.body:
Oh It is. All the assets images, videos, audio was generated through it. Was quite unbelievable for me tbh.


I used chatgpt to give me the prompts to build all the units and audio and video to fit my style and for consistency, and just generated it on scenario one by one.

comments.author: FutureLynx_
comments.body: You did this all without writing a single line of code? Or you had to refactor/review some of it? Looks quite complex.

replies.author: Icy-Requirement5701
replies.body:
Correct..  it was absolutely shocking to me to :)


For what its worth, I found Claude is an order of magnitude better at robust code than Cursor. The harness and ability to manage context definitely produces better results.


I'm an experienced developer so i do know what to expect but everything was prompted. Plan, glance at the plan to make sure it makes engineering sense, and then tell it to implement. I didn't review any code and just ensured the end product worked.
 
I hit a few bugs around the voronoi polygons and leveraged chatgpt to explain how the math worked, and then prompted Claude to look at certain aspects that i suspected were the issue through prompts and it eventually fixed it.


Also being a dev i knew how to optimize aspects.. for eg. let's use a cache so we don't need to recalculate the provinces every time. But again, all prompted.
